title: Live-traffic evaluation of quantized KV across batching regimes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: measure real-world quality and performance trade-offs when applying lossy/compressed representations to the KV cache under continuous batching. This ticket runs an A/B-style evaluation on live traffic slices to understand interaction effects between batching window size, quantized-KV fidelity (FP8/INT8/INT4), and GPU memory fragmentation/eviction behavior. Deliverables: experiment harness, traffic cohorts, dashboards of QoR vs SLO impact, and a safety/handoff policy prototype to avoid customer-visible regressions.
background: We've completed a number of offline quantization probes (int8/int4/fp8) in controlled workloads. Those experiments measured embedding-level RMSE and small-chat perplexity but didn't account for continuous batching, multi-tenant GPU memory pressure, or live request arrival patterns. Anecdotal incidents show transient p99 latency spikes when KV eviction+rehydration coincides with aggressive batching—quantized caches may exacerbate or mask these effects. This work bridges offline fidelity numbers to real production behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Run controlled A/B on two dedicated GPU clusters for 7 days capturing live traffic from 3 product cohorts
Produce dashboards that correlate QoR (token-level mismatch rate, prompt-level pass/fail) to latency p50/p95/p99 and GPU memory reclaimed
Define and demo a runtime safety-harness that promotes degraded requests to higher-fidelity KV (FP8->INT8->FP16) when quality or latency thresholds are triggered
Document clear decision thresholds and recommended defaults for Hosted vs Dedicated customers
experiment_plan: 1) Select three live cohorts: short-chat (avg len 40 tokens), long-chat (avg len 600 tokens), and interactive assistant (bursty token arrivals). 2) Instrument a traffic switcher to route 10% of each cohort to quantized-KV variants: FP8 baseline, INT8 aggressive, INT4 extreme. 3) Sweep batching window sizes: 5ms, 15ms, 50ms, and 150ms. 4) Capture joint metrics: token-quality (token-accuracy vs FP16 baseline), per-request pass/fail for regression test prompts, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU memory used, eviction counts, cold-KV penalty (tokens re-generated after eviction). 5) Introduce synthetic noise: transient memory pressure pulses to observe fallback behavior. 6) Run for 7 days to capture diurnal patterns.
metrics: Token-level mismatch rate (vs FP16 baseline) -- target < 0.5% for FP8, <1.5% for INT8, <4% for INT4
Prompt-level pass rate on golden prompt set -- target degradation < 1% for FP8
p99 latency impact relative to baseline -- target < 10% increase
GPU memory saved (MB) per instance and effective batch size uplift
Eviction rate and cold-KV rehydration penalty (extra tokens emitted)
results_summary: Mid-experiment findings (first 72 hours): FP8 preserved token-level fidelity (avg mismatch 0.34%) across batching windows and delivered ~18% GPU memory reduction vs baseline, allowing median batch size to increase ~12% without breaking p95 latency targets. INT8 showed acceptable fidelity for short-chat (1.2% mismatch) but introduced a 7% p99 latency regression at 150ms batching due to higher eviction frequency on GPUs with >70% fragmentation. INT4 produced significant quality regressions in long-chat cohort (avg mismatch 5.8%) and caused a measurable increase in cold-KV rehydration (token replay up ~0.9% of requests) when memory pressure spikes occurred. Notably, larger batching windows amplify the visibility of rehydration costs because evicted keys affect many requests in a batch. Early safety-harness prototype successfully detected quality drift (prompt-level fail rate >2%) and promoted affected requests to FP8, removing customer-visible regressions in 98% of triggered cases but adding 9% to p95 latency for those promoted requests.
decisions: Stop INT4 for long-chat cohort in Hosted by default; keep INT4 behind an opt-in knob for Dedicated customers with manual SLO acceptance
Adopt FP8 as the recommended default quantized-KV profile for mixed workloads; INT8 remains a candidate for short-chat high-density clusters
Implement a runtime safety-harness that monitors prompt-level regression signals + eviction spikes to promote requests to higher fidelity KV on a per-request basis
Schedule a follow-up to explore more granular per-key fidelity profiling (hot-key high-fidelity, cold-key low-fidelity) in Cycle 11
next_steps: Complete full 7-day run and validate weekend traffic patterns
Refine safety-harness thresholds: move from static >2% prompt-fail threshold to a rolling z-score detector tied to baseline cohort variability
Wire up dashboards (Grafana) with alerting rules for automatic rollback when p99+regression triggers occur
Open PR with runtime changes for per-request promotion and submit design doc for per-key fidelity strategy
Draft customer-facing KB: 'Quantized KV guidance and runtime fallbacks' for Hosted and Dedicated
